$comment: The Liquid glass design (component style look 'liquid'), the same in every pack. Web packs draw it in CSS (bx.css, .bx-look-liquid) on the tokens below; React adds Glisse (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Kelvin Zhang) for the bending lens on its own controls; React Native draws it with a blur view. Glass sits on surfaces that float over content, never behind body text in a field. See docs/MODERNIZATION-PARALLEL-PLAN.md, Liquid glass.

surfaces.$solid: Fields and tables keep a solid fill behind their text; their menus and pop-ups take glass.

bend.how: SVG feDisplacementMap from a per-size lens map, three colour passes for dispersion, over backdrop-filter blur and saturate
bend.where: Chromium only (the live backdrop); Safari and Firefox show frost and the lit rim without bending

fallbacks.prefers-reduced-transparency: a solid surface (--bx-surface) with the rim
fallbacks.forced-colors: the system colours, no tint, a 1px border
fallbacks.prefers-reduced-motion: the glass stays still: no lens following the pointer, no stretch on press
fallbacks.no-backdrop-filter: a solid surface at 92% with the rim

rules: Text on glass passes WCAG AA contrast over the busiest backdrop the screen shows, in both themes
No lens follows moving content: glass is static over its backdrop, so no frame loop runs (Glisse's follow loop is for marked, moving content)
At most a few large glass surfaces per screen; dialogs and sheets use one
